messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall — elevated fncall/tool-invoke error rate (service: fn-invoke-proxy). Spike detected 08:12 UTC; increased 5xx and dropped requests. Severity: P2. O11y: https://o11y.redwood.example/graphs/abc123 :rotating_light:

sara: taking this — will triage now. anyone on-call with infra access?

mike: i'm live. grabbing logs from the proxy pool. initial look: surge of long-running structured-output streaming sessions, KV cache pressure and worker OOM / restart loops. 95th p90 latency for fncall up ~3x.

jordan: customer impact? any paid tenants affected or just trials?

lee: paging from support — several trial + some small SaaS customers seeing repeated bot-level failures when using agent-style tool calls. top affected tenants: tenant-197, tenant-820, tenant-34. No enterprise SLA hits reported yet.

mike: logs show a few tenants generating continuous tool-call loops; prefix-KV growth and sustained heavy token generation causing runtime backpressure. It's saturating the fn-invoke-proxy pool.

sara: we should do a scoped mitigation that reduces blast radius without full rollback. proposal: 1) apply soft per-tenant fncall RPS caps; 2) disable structured-output streaming (chunked JSON) for free & trial tiers; 3) gate function/tool-calling behind feature-flag for hosted tier as temporary fallback.

jordan: agree — prefer targeted caps over full disable. need comms plan for tenants that hit the cap.

mike: actionable steps:
- apply global soft RPS cap at proxy: 5 RPS per tenant for function calls (enforced token-level).
- add burst allowance = 10 for existing dedicated tenants flagged as "trusted".
- flip streaming responses off for plans: free, trial.
- add a runtime knob to downgrade toolcalls to no-op warnings if over cap.

ops-bot: action created: MIT-2024-3387 — mitigation: fncall-rps-cap + streaming-disable. Assigned to mike, sara.

sara: i'll update status page & internal incident doc. putting a quick note in #customer-facing: "We're applying temporary caps to tool/function calls to reduce errors; customers will see reduced throughput for scripted agent workloads."

mike: implementing now. commands i will run (internal):
```
# set proxy limit (applies immediately)
redwoodctl proxy set-limit --service fn-invoke-proxy --scope tenant --rps 5 --burst 10

# disable streaming for plan tiers
redwoodctl feature-toggle set --flag streaming_structured_output --tiers free,trial --value false

# gate fncalls for hosted temporarily
redwoodctl feature-toggle set --flag enable_fn_calling --env hosted --value gated
```

sara: noted. mike - please post confirmation after each step. i'll push status update when the first two are live.

mike: limit applied to proxy cluster alpha & beta. see logs:
```
2024-05-15T08:20:14Z proxy-alpha fncall: limit set tenant_rps=5 burst=10
2024-05-15T08:20:17Z proxy-beta  fncall: streaming disabled tiers=free,trial
```

lee: support loop — I'll proactively message top affected tenants with the temporary mitigation note and offer a short troubleshooting walkthrough. drafting now.

jordan: i'll prepare a short public blurb in case we need wider comms. want to avoid causing alarm — emphasize targeted mitigation and next steps.

mike: added transient metric emit for "fncall_rate_limited" and an alert to watch reduction in proxy errors. watching dashboard: https://o11y.redwood.example/d/fncall-metrics?org=redwood

ops-bot: log action: MIT-2024-3387 step=apply-caps actor=mike status=done ts=1718504440

sara: status page updated: "We are applying temporary per-tenant caps on function/tool calls for hosted free/trial tiers to mitigate elevated error rates. We are monitoring and will post updates."

mike: after caps, proxy 5xxs dropped ~60% and queue depth reduced. CPU on worker hosts climbed for a bit then stabilized. p95 latency down from 1.2s to 0.6s for fncall proxy.

jordan: good progress. what about structured-output? any functional regressions for enterprise customers?

mike: streaming disabled only for free/trial via feature toggle. enterprise/dedicated unaffected. fallback behavior: clients get synchronous JSON post-processed responses (no chunking) — should be compatible.

sara: next steps:
- monitor for 30m 
- if stable, gradually relax caps for trusted tenants 
- if errors resurge, escalate to disable_fn_calls global and run rollback plan

lee: will notify customers impacted by caps and include mitigation ETA (30-60m).

mike: setting watch for 30m and will hold handoff. anyone else pick up after me?

sara: i'll take the 30m watch after you. mike — leave notes in the incident doc about exact commands & timestamps.

ops-bot: MIT-2024-3387 update: monitoring metrics show error-rate down 62% and rate-limited events at 420 across tenants in first 10m.

mike: leaving runbook notes:
```
# rollback if needed
redwoodctl feature-toggle set --flag enable_fn_calling --env hosted --value true
redwoodctl proxy clear-limit --service fn-invoke-proxy --scope tenant
redwoodctl feature-toggle set --flag streaming_structured_output --tiers free,trial --value true
```

sara: thanks — handing over watch to me. next update at 08:50 UTC or sooner if anything changes. tagging @jordan and @lee for comms. :white_check_mark:

jordan: acknowledged. I'll standby for customer comms and post a short note to partners if enterprise usage changes.

lee: support message sent to top affected tenants. no escalations so far.

incident-bot: Reminder: oncall handoff in 30m to sara.

sara: confirming watch started. closing active mitigation thread — moving to incident doc for postmortem notes.

mike: thanks all. follow-up: we should discuss permanent throttling & better KV eviction heuristics in next infra triage.

ops-bot: MIT-2024-3387 status: mitigated -> monitoring. closed by sara at ts=1718504620
